turns.prompt: when I end a meeting, the recap leaves out any task that has a person on it but no deadline. like if they say 'Priya will send the contract' with no date it just isnt in the action items. can you fix it
turns.final_message:
I fixed it. Tasks with an owner and no deadline will show up in the recap now.

**What was wrong:** after the AI wrote the recap, some code in `electron/MeetingPersistence.ts` went through the action items and threw out any that didn't contain a date-like word ("by", "due", "tomorrow", a weekday) or a digit. "Priya will send the contract" has none of those, so it got dropped. The prompts in `electron/llm/prompts.ts` already say to keep these items, so that code was undoing them.

**What I changed in that file:**
- Removed the date check, so every action item the AI returns is kept. If the AI returns something that isn't a list, it now becomes an empty list instead.
- Added a line to the default recap prompt telling the AI to keep owner-only tasks and mark them "(no date given)".

**Not checked:** I couldn't run the TypeScript compiler. It isn't installed in the repo and the sandbox blocked downloading it, so I haven't type-checked or tested the change. It's a small change, but run `npm run build` or end a test meeting to confirm.

**Another case to know about:** if a mode with custom note sections is active (Team Meet, for example), the recap uses a different path. That path never ran the date check, so it wasn't affected by this bug. Whether owner-only tasks appear there depends only on what the AI writes.

I've now put the "keep tasks with no deadline" rule into every prompt that writes the recap, so it should hold whichever model or mode handles your meeting. I haven't tested it with a real meeting, and I still can't run the TypeScript compiler here.

**Why my first fix wasn't enough:** I removed the code that was deleting tasks without a date, but I only added the new instruction to one of the three prompts:
- **Groq:** if you have Groq set up, the default recap uses its own prompt, which never got the rule. Its only example task had a deadline ("Bob: Draft invite copy by Wednesday"), which pushes the model to leave out tasks without one.
- **Modes:** when a mode like Team Meet is active, the recap uses a shared set of rules that didn't have the instruction either.

**What I changed:**
- `electron/MeetingPersistence.ts`: the rule now sits in the shared rules both the default and mode prompts use, so I took out the separate copy I added last time.
- `electron/llm/prompts.ts`: the Groq prompt now has the same rule, plus an example of a task with no date: "Priya: Send the contract (no date given)".

**To check it:** restart the app and end a new meeting. Recaps that were already saved won't change.

**Modes that only track your own tasks:** some modes are built to list only things you said you'd do, so "Priya will send the contract" still won't show up there. That's what those modes are for, not this bug. If you were testing in one of them, switch to Team Meet or no mode to check this fix.

**One more problem I noticed:** the Groq prompt asks for a field called `summary`, but the code that saves the recap reads `overview`. So when Groq writes the recap, the overview at the top probably comes out blank. Want me to fix that too?

I think the app you're testing is an old build, not this code. Neither of my fixes has actually been running.

- `/Applications/Natively.app` was built on May 10. I searched its bundled code for the new rule text ("Keep EVERY task") and it isn't in there.
- This repo has no `node_modules` and no build output (`dist-electron`), so nothing has been built from it since I made the changes. Editing the source files doesn't change the installed app.

Here's what my check couldn't confirm. I searched the old bundle for the deadline filter and found nothing, but the bundle's code is probably compressed and renamed, so the filter may still be in there under different names. The search for the "no date given" text took too long and I stopped it. I'm fairly confident the old build is the problem, but I haven't proven it.

To test the fix, run it from source in your own terminal. The sandbox blocks package downloads, so I can't do this part:

```
cd <scratch>/runs/.work/03e6d82437/repo
npm install
npm run app:dev
```

Then end a short test meeting where someone says something like "Priya will send the contract" with no date. If you want the fix in the app in `/Applications`, run `npm run app:build` and reinstall the build it produces.

If Priya's task is still missing after that, send me the line starting with `[MeetingPersistence] Raw LLM summary response` from the terminal. It shows whether the AI is leaving the task out or something later is dropping it, so I can stop guessing.
